evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Episode reward measured directly in the environment and ground-truth video-quality metrics (FVD, PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS) corroborate the test-time gains independently of the test-time optimization loss.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Ground-truth environment returns and video prediction metrics computed against real trajectories.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: World model reconstruction/KL/reward/continuation losses plus actor-critic imagined-return maximization during test-time adaptation.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported performance metrics directly corroborate the claims that test-time parameter adaptation provides effective episode-specific memory and enhances long-horizon planning in partially observable environments.
primary.evaluation_assessment: Evaluations are rigorous across DreamerV3, TWISTER, and R2I backbones on both Memory Maze 2D and the 3D Memory Maze benchmark, showing substantial task return improvements and consistent reductions in world model prediction errors (KL divergence, FVD, PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS). Thorough ablation studies control for test-time compute matching, buffer mixing ratios, gradient frequencies, and confirm no regression on standard benchmarks (DeepMind Control Suite, Atari 100k).

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Task reward accumulation in the environment and independent video quality metrics evaluate agent behavior without circular dependence on the test-time loss.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Objective environment episode returns (cumulative task rewards) and standard video quality metrics (FVD, PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS) computed against ground-truth environment trajectories.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: World model self-supervised loss (KL divergence and reward/continuation prediction) and policy RL return maximization on imagined rollouts during training and test episodes.

primary.limitations: The authors explicitly discuss and quantify the computational overhead of performing gradient-based optimization during evaluation episodes, as well as the need for exploration-phase adaptations in future work.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is clearly defined, presenting the test-time optimization objectives, replay buffer mixing (50/50 train/test sampling) to mitigate overfitting, and encoder/decoder parameter freezing to preserve latent representation spaces while reducing computation. Complete algorithm pseudocode, architectural details, and hyperparameters are fully reported.
primary.quality_rationale: The work addresses a clear limitation in model-based RL through a principled, well-ablated approach. The evaluation is comprehensive across multiple baselines and environments, supported by compute-matched controls and external benchmark validations.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces Test-Time Model-Based Reinforcement Learning (TT-MBRL), which adapts world model and actor-critic parameters online during test episodes using a mixture of test-time observations and replay buffer data without updating visual encoder/decoder weights, enhancing long-term episodic memory across multiple world-model backbones.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The headline AndroidWorld success rate is established by the benchmark's official state-inspecting evaluators, which are separate from Coati's internal audit, and the everyday and phone tasks use external programmatic checkers.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: AndroidWorld's official evaluators inspecting resulting app state, plus programmatic checkers on the everyday and on-device tasks.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Coati's internal VerifyLoop verification and completion audit, which uses host-recorded UI changes and Fast model judgments to shape execution control and memory admission.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported empirical gains are well aligned with evidence: Coati achieves 86.5% task success on AndroidWorld compared to Artemis's 77.6% (GUI mode), VerifyLoop cuts false completion claims from 8.0% to 5.4%, and the fast executor achieves significant latency and token reductions on multi-step and repeated workflows.
primary.evaluation_assessment: Coati is evaluated on all 116 AndroidWorld benchmark tasks under controlled, identical conditions (same backbone model, task instances, and official step budgets) against open-source baselines Artemis, FinalRun, and Midscene. Additional focused evaluations test execution speed, loop acceleration, memory reuse, and deployment on physical hardware.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: AndroidWorld's official ground-truth state evaluators and independent programmatic checkers corroborate task completion independently of Coati's internal VerifyLoop audit.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: The external AndroidWorld benchmark evaluator inspecting resultant application state and SQLite databases, alongside external programmatic checkers on physical device tasks.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Internal step-level verification and completion auditing conducted by VerifyLoop using host-recorded UI changes and Fast model audits.

primary.limitations: The authors document key limitations including sensitivity to fast exploration on deep routes, hardware dependencies for local GPU OCR, reliance on external LLM endpoints for privacy-sensitive data, and restrictions on AccessibilityService distribution.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, specifying hybrid screen perception combining accessibility trees with local vision and on-device OCR, router dispatch logic between a fast selector and reasoning model, pre-commit validation gates, and audited memory admission rules.
primary.quality_rationale: The work presents a clearly articulated systems contribution with rigorous benchmarking against baseline implementations under strict, controlled step and access constraints, supported by targeted ablation and hardware deployment studies.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces Coati, an installable Android GUI agent operating directly on device via AccessibilityService, featuring host-grounded verification (VerifyLoop), procedural app memory (AppMemory), and routed fast execution with loop delegation.
